what_it_does: Modern AI hardware is increasingly built by combining multiple specialized chips ('chiplets') on a shared base layer called an active interposer — think of the interposer as a sophisticated circuit board that also contains its own logic. The interposer carries the network that lets chiplets talk to each other, but a single fixed wiring layout cannot efficiently handle the huge variety of traffic patterns that arise across different AI workloads. EIGEN adds two cooperating network layers on the interposer: one that can be statically reconfigured per application to create the best topology for that workload, and one that dynamically reroutes packets at runtime when congestion appears. A reinforcement learning agent — software that learns good routing choices through trial and reward — controls the dynamic layer, balancing latency and link load.
